    Finite cogeneration tests for an endofinite module #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.IsEndofinite.exists_fg_mutual_embeddings {R : Type u} [Ring R] {N : ModuleCat R} (hN : IsEndofinite N) (hs : ∀ (G : ModuleCat R) (a : CategoryTheory.Retract G N), CategoryTheory.Indecomposable G → Module.Finite R ↑G) :
    ∃ (M : FGModuleCat R), Function.Injective ⇑(LinearMap.pi fun (f : ↑N →ₗ[R] ↑M) => f) ∧ Function.Injective ⇑(LinearMap.pi fun (f : ↑M →ₗ[R] ↑N) => f)

    If every indecomposable summand is finitely generated, a single finitely generated module has the same cogeneration tests as N. Each module embeds in a product of copies of the other.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.finite_cogenerator_or_grain_retract {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsArtinianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] {N : ModuleCat R} (he : IsEndofinite N) (hs : SplitsOnCogeneratedModules k N) :
    (∃ (M : FGModuleCat R), perpendicularToModule N = perpendicularToModule M.obj ∧ cogeneratedByModule N = cogeneratedByModule M.obj) ∨ ∃ (G : ModuleCat R), Nonempty (CategoryTheory.Retract G N) ∧ IsGenericGrain k G

    An endofinite splitting witness either has the same finite cogenerated modules and left perpendicular as one finite module, or has a generic grain as an indecomposable summand.
